Landed. stated_total_deltas on Part: a per-column, per-page declaration of a discrepancy in the DOCUMENT's own arithmetic. No global epsilon, no per-rule fuzz.

SHAPE. StatedTotalDelta{Column (1-based, matching how CheckTotals numbers columns when it reports a mismatch, so a failure message can be pasted into a declaration), Cents (STATED MINUS MAPPED, in cents always), Note (required)}. The parser refuses an out-of-range column, a duplicate column, a skipped column, a zero delta and a missing or whitespace-only note -- so a malformed declaration fails when the file is READ, not when it is applied.

BEHAVIOUR. CheckTotals accepts exactly the declared figure and nothing else. Three failure modes, told apart in the message: an undeclared discrepancy fails as before; a declared column off by a different amount fails naming both figures; and a declared column that now TIES EXACTLY also fails, telling the author to remove the declaration. That last one is the direction nothing else would catch -- if the city reissues the page with the arithmetic corrected, a tolerance would silently keep passing while the declaration became a false claim about the document.

THE ARITHMETIC, carried in the test rather than described. Budget Book p127's thirteen Property Taxes rows, from the committed fixture: FY2023-24 Actual 58,179,467 against a printed 58,179,468 (+1); FY2024-25 60,621,418, FY2025-26 64,143,762, FY2026-27 67,416,730, all exact. Three of four columns tying exactly is what makes the fourth the document's rounding rather than our read -- a misread row would not land on three columns and miss one by a dollar.

REPORTING. TotalsResult.Declared and Report.ColumnsTiedByDeclaration, printed whenever non-zero: '1 of those columns ties only to a declared delta in the document's own arithmetic'. A column that ties on the city's rounding must not be counted as one that ties exactly; that is the same principle as pkg/cmd/build/report.go's UNCHECKED lines.

  dependency skips the dependent, so one guard covers both.

  database fetched at run time rather than on the commit, so the same tree can
  be green today and red tomorrow. The published artefact is static HTML, CSS
  and vendored d3 -- no Go ships -- so nothing it reports can reach a visitor,
  and gating publication on it would make republishing fail for reasons
  unrelated to the site.

- pages-deploy carries its own `concurrency: {group: pages, cancel-in-progress:
  false}`. The workflow-wide group is per-ref and does not cancel on main,
  which is right for CI but would let two quick pushes race for a single Pages
  deployment.

- Job-level permissions REPLACE the workflow block rather than extend it, so
  pages-deploy grants exactly pages:write and id-token:write and no contents:
  deploy-pages reads the uploaded artefact, not the repository. pages-build
  keeps the inherited contents:read floor.

THIS BEAD'S OWN STATED MECHANISM WAS WRONG, and the correction matters beyond this bead. It said deadcode does not flag Slice 'because the tests reach it'. deadcode WITHOUT -test does not look at tests at all, so that cannot be it. The real cause is RTA method over-approximation: a method counts as reachable when its receiver is a runtime type and any interface dispatch in the program has a matching signature, and signatures like func() bool match spuriously. That is why the same audit (9f1df6d) also missed geom.(*Grid).Gutter and the three iostreams TTY accessors, all of which have zero references of any kind. A method-level SELECTOR grep is not redundant with deadcode; recorded as a memory.

THE PRINCIPLE THAT DECIDES IT, and it is why the measurement was never the question: everything is checked on the Go side and trusted on the JavaScript side; JavaScript decides only what to RENDER, based on what the user does. That is AGENTS.md's 'Go vets, JavaScript renders' applied to a ribbon exactly as it was applied to a derived mark's cents.

WHY CANDIDATE (b) IS REFUSED RATHER THAN MERELY NOT CHOSEN. Shipping only the 96 ribbons no document prints, and having the client look the other 1,486 up by (source, target, kind), is cheaper on the wire -- +2,054 gzipped against +20,699 -- but it puts a RULE on the client: which ribbons are in the file and which are to be found elsewhere. A rule the client applies is a rule that can be wrong in silence, and a ribbon Go wrongly believed was printed would be drawn at a value the client invented. The saving buys a second place where a published figure is decided.
